Consult Summary:  
19-year-old female presents with a one-week history of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic aching pain, and recent onset of pink-tinged urine, consistent with probable urinary tract infection (UTI).

History:  
- Presenting complaint: Burning pain on urination, increased urinary frequency, suprapubic aching pain, and pink discoloration of urine noted today.  
- Timeline: Symptoms started just under one week ago, with gradual persistence; no improvement reported.  
- Pain localized to the lower abdomen, worse on urination, described as aching rather than crampy.  
- No radiation of pain to back or flanks.  
- No fever, nausea, or vomiting.  
- Bowel habits unchanged; known history of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) with variable stool consistency and frequency, no new symptoms.  
- No vaginal discharge reported.  
- Last menstrual period two weeks ago.  
- Sexually active in a stable relationship, on combined oral contraceptive pill; last unprotected intercourse approximately one to two weeks ago.  
- Social history: Lives in university halls with a flatmate, family lives nearby outside London; occasional social alcohol use, no smoking, tried cannabis once 1.5 weeks ago.  
- No other systemic symptoms reported.

Past Medical History:  
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) with associated bowel habit irregularity.  
- No other medical conditions reported.

Medications:  
- Combined oral contraceptive pill (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Medication for IBS starting with "M" (name, dose/route/frequency not documented), described as for crampy pain.  
- Allergy: Clindamycin noted to cause adverse reaction.

Social History:  
- University student studying English, living in halls with a flatmate.  
- Occasional social alcohol use.  
- Experimental cannabis use once 1.5 weeks ago; advised to avoid regular use.  
- No tobacco use.

Family History:  
- No known family history of urinary tract or kidney problems.

Physical Examination:  
- No examination findings documented.  
- No vital signs recorded.

Investigations:  
- Urine sample recommended to be collected at clinic for microscopy, culture, and sensitivity.

Assessment & Plan:  

Issue 1: Urinary tract infection (probable cystitis)  
- Assessment: Typical presentation of uncomplicated UTI with dysuria, frequency, suprapubic pain, and pink-tinged urine; no systemic features to suggest upper tract involvement.  
- Plan:  
  • Prescribe short course antibiotic therapy options discussed: Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin (3-day course); specific antibiotic choice not documented.  
  • Advise increased fluid intake for adequate hydration.  
  • Recommend symptomatic treatment with Paracetamol for pain relief.  
  • Urine sample to be collected at clinic for laboratory evaluation to confirm diagnosis and antibiotic sensitivities.  
  • Patient advised to return if symptoms worsen or do not improve within one week.  
  • Alert patient to seek urgent medical advice if fever, flank pain, or vomiting develop.

Issue 2: IBS (background condition)  
- Assessment: Stable with usual bowel symptoms, no new issues currently.  
- Plan: Continue current IBS medication.

Issue 3: Cannabis use (social)  
- Assessment: Single experimental use; no direct relation to current symptoms but counseling provided.  
- Plan: Strongly advise against regular cannabis use for general health.

General Plan:  
- Follow up based on urine culture results or clinical progression.  
- Educate patient on signs of complicated infection needing prompt review.

Document Quality & Notes:  
- No vital signs or physical exam findings documented; expected elements for UTI evaluation missing.  
- Medication names incompletely documented; IBS medication not clearly identified.  
- Allergy to Clindamycin recorded, no dose or reaction details.  
- No conflicts noted in transcript.  
- Transcript clear, complete, and audible throughout.
